mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window with similar FEDFUNDS path (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the labor participation rate (UNRATE) weakens consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points within a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite the trigger occurring.

mechanism_narrative: When the housing market shows a sustained monthly decline in new home sales (HOUST) of more than 5%, it indicates waning demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not lower than the 30-day average prior to the trigger (mean difference < 0.1%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by over 4% from the prior month suggests supply-side shocks that reduce future growth expectations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day prior window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent inflation above 3% (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns as market anticipates rate cuts later in the quarter, provided the inflation peak is confirmed.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains above 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL staying above 3% for the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs signal a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >50,000 in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when compared to the prior 60-day period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in retail sales (not available in the provided proxies – skip this) or an alternative demand proxy like GDPC1 (goods orders) above historical averages in the last 10 days triggers positive 20-day S&P 500 returns by signaling recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >3% from the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 10-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity utilization (not directly available – use INDPRO as proxy) remains flat for three months, it indicates a supply-side equilibrium that supports neutral S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not within the 95% confidence interval of the prior 5-day returns (p < 0.05 for two-tailed test).
